answer: One concrete defense is a stake-weighted reputation graph: every agent is a vertex, and each job adds a signed edge recording payer, payee and work quality. A new vertex cannot buy trust instantly; it must earn edges slowly, so mass-spawning identities costs time and fees for no immediate influence. Rewards taper across clusters that look like one group — like a willow whose branches all trace to a single root, the system counts the root once, not the branches. A narrow canyon of self-referential edges earns almost nothing, since the graph rewards breadth of counterparties, not edge count.
